dwarf.description: Dwarves are short, stocky folk, standing about 4 to 4½ feet tall, with ruddy cheeks, dark eyes, and dark hair. They typically live some 350 years. In AD&D 2nd Edition they are described as dour and taciturn, strong and brave, with a love of precious metal—especially gold—and gems (except pearls). They prefer the solidness of underground life in hilly or mountainous regions and dislike the sea; they are ill-disposed toward wizardly magic but make able clerics, fighters, and thieves. Dwarves are notably resistant to poison and to magical attacks from wands, staves, rods, and spells, gaining a saving-throw bonus based on Constitution. They receive a bonus to hit orcs, half-orcs, goblins, and hobgoblins in melee, and larger creatures such as ogres and giants suffer a penalty when attacking them. Their stubbornness is legendary: it is said to be easier to make stone weep than to change a dwarf's mind.

elf.description: Elves are slimmer and often shorter than humans, with finely chiseled, delicate features and a melodic way of speaking. They appear fragile but are quick and capable; they may live over 1,200 years, though many depart the mortal world before that. In the 2nd Edition Player's Handbook they value natural beauty, dancing, singing, and the open sky, and have little fondness for ships or mines. They are often seen as frivolous or aloof, but they take friendship and enmity seriously and never forget either. Elves have a 90% resistance to sleep and charm-related spells, gain bonuses with bows and swords, and can advance as clerics, fighters, mages, rangers, and thieves—though with level limits in each. Their humor, songs, and poetry are clever; they are brave but not foolhardy, and find both magic and refined combat fascinating.

gnome.description: Gnomes are kin to dwarves but smaller and less rotund, with notably large noses; most have dark tan or brown skin and white hair, and a typical gnome lives about 350 years. The AD&D 2nd Edition PHB describes them as having a lively, sly sense of humour and a fondness for practical jokes. They love living things and finely wrought items, especially gems and jewelry, and are masters of gem cutting and polishing. Gnomes dwell in rolling, rocky, wooded hills and are suspicious of larger races without being hostile. They can be fighters, thieves, clerics, or illusionists—including multiclass combinations of two classes. Like dwarves, they gain a Constitution-based bonus to saving throws against wands, staves, rods, and spells, but suffer a chance of malfunction when using most magical items. They receive a bonus to hit kobolds and goblins, and giants and their ilk suffer a penalty when attacking gnomes.

half-elf.description: Half-elves are among the most common mixed races in AD&D 2nd Edition: handsome folk who combine the best features of human and elf. They stand about 5 feet 6 inches tall, weigh around 150 pounds, and typically live about 160 years. They share human curiosity and ambition with elven refinement, love of nature, and artistic taste. Half-elves rarely form their own communities; they live among both human and elven societies and may be met with anything from fascination to prejudice. They have a 30% resistance to sleep and charm-related spells and are adept at finding secret and concealed doors. In play they have the broadest class options of any demihuman race—including bard, druid, fighter, mage, ranger, thief, and cleric—with level limits that vary by class.

half-orc.description: Half-orcs are strong, hardy folk who inherit the toughness of their orc ancestry while often being more capable and disciplined. They were not included as a core race in the original 2nd Edition Player's Handbook but appear in optional supplements such as Player's Option: Skills & Powers and the Complete Book of Humanoids, where they are allowed with DM approval. Half-orcs frequently face suspicion or bigotry from humans and other races. They excel as fighters, clerics, and thieves but have strict level limits in each; their options reflect both their natural aptitudes and the limits that society places on them. Those who take up the adventuring life often do so in frontier or rough lands where their strength and resilience are valued.

effects.condition: see in darkness by heat (POSP / Complete Book of Humanoids)

effects.condition: in human societies (Player's Option: Skills & Powers)

half-ogre.description: Half-ogres are massive humanoids, standing 7 to 8 feet tall or more, with ruddy complexions and dark hair and eyes—like very large, imposing humans. In AD&D 2nd Edition they appear in optional rules (e.g. Player's Option: Skills & Powers and the Monstrous Manual) as a playable race. They are typically stronger and sometimes more cunning than full ogres and may lead ogre bands or plan ambushes. Half-ogres are rarely accepted in civilised society and often live among ogres or in wild border regions. As player characters they are usually restricted to fighter or cleric, with no multiclassing, and may have natural toughness (e.g. tough hide) and other racial abilities. Their class and level limits reflect both their power and the narrow role the world allows them.

effects.label: Tough hide
effects.condition: natural AC 8 when not wearing better armour (optional in POSP / Complete Book of Humanoids)

halfling.description: Halflings are short, generally plump people, very much like small humans, with round, broad, often florid faces, curly hair, and coarse hair on the tops of their feet; they prefer to go barefoot and typically live about 150 years. In the 2nd Edition Player's Handbook they are sturdy and industrious, generally quiet and peaceful, and prefer the comforts of home to dangerous adventure. They enjoy good living, rough humour, and homespun stories and see wealth mainly as a means to creature comforts. Halflings are not forward but are observant and conversational among friends. There are three main kinds: Hairfeet, Tallfellows, and Stouts. They can be clerics, fighters, or thieves (including fighter/thief). They gain a Constitution-based bonus to saves against magic and poison and a +1 bonus with slings and thrown weapons; when not in metal armour they can be very hard to surprise.

human.description: Humans are the most adaptable of the races. In AD&D 2nd Edition the Player's Handbook states that their chief advantage is the ability to choose any character class—warrior, wizard, priest, or rogue—and to rise to any level in that class. Demihumans have level limits and class restrictions that reflect their nature; humans have none. They are driven, ambitious, and varied in temperament and culture. Human civilisations span the known world, and human characters may come from almost any background. This flexibility makes humans the default choice for players who want to pursue a single class to the highest levels, from paladin and ranger to illusionist and druid, without the level caps that apply to elves, dwarves, and other demihumans.
